title: Lock files and checksum files
summary: Twenty snippets of package-lock.json, yarn.lock, go.sum and similar dependency lock files, each line carrying an integrity hash.
rationale: Integrity hashes are long, random-looking, base64 or hexadecimal, and public. Lock files are large and committed in nearly every project, so any weakness here multiplies.
unscopedReason: Authored detector and arrival-target metadata intentionally assign no credential family; this fixture remains a global benchmark control.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged. The hashes verify published packages and are public by design. Sources added under the maintainer decision recorded in ADR 0019 (issue #142) show each value's role (an integrity or content hash, a revision identifier); none states that the value is not a credential, so the basis stays project-policy.

sources.supports: integrity is a sha512 or sha1 Standard Subresource Integrity string for the artifact unpacked at the location.
go.sum records h1: hashes (hash of module content, base64).
Hash-checking mode uses hashes embedded in a requirements file (--hash=sha256:...) to protect against remote tampering and network issues.
